title: Second Helvetic Confession: sins unequal; Pelagians and Jovinians condemned
source_text: VI. Super hac re diserta est Confessio Helvetica posterior, quae in Confessionum Harmonia, sive Syntagmate habetur, & quam subscriptione sua comprobarunt, non solum Ecclesiae vicinae Tigurinorum & Bernensium, aliorumque quorum est Confessio; sed & remotiores Hungaricae, Polonicae, Scoticae, Gallicae, aliaque Reformatae. Nam in ista Confessione haec ad verbum leguntur, Fatemur non omnia peccata esse aequalia, licet ex eodem corruptionis & infidelitatis fonte fluant; sed alia aliis esse graviora, sicut Dominus dixerat, tolerabilius fore Sodoma, quam civitati quae verbum Evangelii contemneret. Damnamus ergo omnes qui his contraria docuerunt; in primis Pelagium, cum omnibus Pelagianis, una cum Jovinianistis, peccata cum Stoicis paria facientibus.
pass_a_gloss: On this matter the Second Helvetic Confession is explicit, which is had in the Harmony or Syntagma of Confessions, and which not only the neighboring churches of the Zurichers and Bernese and others whose Confession it is, but also the more remote Hungarian, Polish, Scottish, French, and other Reformed churches confirmed by their subscription. For in that Confession these words are read: We confess that not all sins are equal, although they flow from the same fountain of corruption and unbelief; but that some are graver than others, as the Lord had said that it would be more tolerable for Sodom than for the city that despised the word of the Gospel. We therefore condemn all who have taught the contrary; first of all Pelagius, with all the Pelagians, together with the Jovinianists, who with the Stoics make sins equal.
pass_b_english: Helvetic II—and its Reformed subscribers—deny equal sins and cite harsher judgment than Sodom’s.
Pelagians and Jovinianists who Stoicize vice-parity are expressly damned.

choices.why: Corpus title for collected Reformed confessions.
